findings.evidence: Gotcha 'Never rebase onto local `main` ..., never `git pull` ..., never `git merge`' repeats step 3 line 19 'Rebase onto the remote ref, never local `main`; never `git pull` or `git merge`'
findings.fix: Keep the reasons in the Gotchas line. In step 3, cut the sentence to 'Rebase onto the remote ref (see Gotchas)' so the same rule is not stated twice.

findings.evidence: The preamble packs argument parsing, fork/upstream base selection ('`base=origin`, except fork PRs: if an `upstream` remote exists ...') and the stop rule into one paragraph before the numbered phases
findings.fix: Make base selection its own numbered phase 0 ('Resolve target and base'), with the upstream/fork decision as a short if/else. The decision then gets a checkpoint like the other phases.

findings.evidence: Gotchas cover lease disarming and ours/theirs, but not stacked branches: other local branches built on `$branch` keep the pre-rebase commits after the rewrite
findings.fix: Add a gotcha: 'If other local branches are stacked on this one, a plain rebase strands them on the old commits; mention `git rebase --update-refs` or list the dependent branches (`git branch --contains "$orig"`) in the report.'

findings.evidence: 'If `$remote` is set and `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$remote" "$orig"` fails, the remote has commits the local branch lacks: stop' — after a run whose push failed in step 5 (network, hook), or after a manual local rebase, the remote holds the pre-rebase copies, so a rerun always stops here with no way forward
findings.fix: Before stopping, compare patches with `git range-diff` or `git cherry "$orig" "$remote"`. If every remote-only commit has an equivalent patch in `$orig` (an earlier rebase that was never pushed), continue to the push with the lease on `$remote`. Stop only when real new remote commits exist.

findings.evidence: The force-push confirmation and the merge-commit question are asked even when `$base/$target` is already an ancestor of `$branch`, where the rebase is a no-op and nothing gets force-pushed
findings.fix: After the fetch in step 2, add: 'If `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$base/$target" "$branch"` succeeds, report that the branch is already up to date with <base>/<target> and stop without asking or pushing.'
